title: The Effect of Using MatGPT on Mathematical Proficiency among Undergraduate Students
venue: International Journal of Information and Education Technology
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether using MatGPT, a MATLAB-integrated interface to OpenAI’s ChatGPT, improves undergraduate students’ mathematical proficiency when solving differential equations. The authors focus on a broader question relevant to AI in mathematics education: whether an AI-supported environment can improve not just overall performance but also specific strands of proficiency such as conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, strategic competence, and adaptive reasoning.

The intervention compared three instructional approaches for the same differential equations content: traditional paper-and-pen instruction, MATLAB without AI support, and MatGPT. The study was conducted with 94 undergraduate students enrolled in a Differential Equation course at a private Jordanian university, divided into one control group and two experimental groups. The treatment lasted three weeks, and teachers received a two-hour workshop before implementation on how to use MatGPT and score student work with the mathematical proficiency rubric.

Results showed that the MatGPT group outperformed the MATLAB and traditional groups on overall mathematical proficiency, with statistically significant gains especially in procedural fluency, strategic competence, and adaptive reasoning. Conceptual understanding did not differ significantly across groups in the adjusted analyses, which the authors interpret as reflecting students’ prior exposure to differential equation concepts before the intervention. The paper concludes that MatGPT may be a useful AI-supported tool for enhancing mathematical proficiency in university mathematics instruction, while also noting practical challenges such as teacher training and digital security needs.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental comparison with pretest adjustment (MANCOVA) and a clearly described intervention and outcome rubric, which supports moderate credibility. However, it is not randomized at the individual level and is limited to a single university course context, so it falls short of blue-tier rigor.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports a medium-to-large positive effect on overall mathematical proficiency (eta^2=0.36) and sizable gains on several subskills. Because the effects are substantial and directly relevant to mathematics learning, the paper merits a blue impact rating despite the nonrandomized design.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT embedded within MATLAB (MatGPT) to provide step-by-step conversational assistance, hints, immediate feedback, and solution verification for solving differential equations in a university mathematics course.
Traditional MATLAB-based computational instruction for solving and visualizing differential equations without the ChatGPT conversational layer.

finding.finding_summary: Using MatGPT improved overall mathematical proficiency for undergraduate students solving differential equations compared with MATLAB and traditional instruction. The adjusted mean overall proficiency was 59.03 for MatGPT versus 50.49 for MATLAB and 40.22 for traditional teaching; the treatment effect was statistically significant (F=16.65, p<=0.05, eta^2=0.36) in a quasi-experimental sample of n=94.
finding.measure: Mathematical proficiency test on five differential equations scored across conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, strategic competence, and adaptive reasoning

finding.finding_summary: MatGPT outperformed both MATLAB and traditional teaching on procedural fluency, strategic competence, and adaptive reasoning, while conceptual understanding showed no significant treatment effect in the omnibus model. Reported effect sizes were moderate-to-large for procedural fluency (eta^2=0.23), strategic competence (eta^2=0.26), and adaptive reasoning (eta^2=0.33), with adjusted means favoring MatGPT (63.76, 34.24, and 49.02, respectively).
finding.measure: Mathematical proficiency strand scores: procedural fluency, strategic competence, adaptive reasoning, and conceptual understanding
